finding: Both arms of the anchor are recorded -- the genuine bundle verifies with the store unmounted and no adapter imported, and the same call on a mutated subject digest is rejected with subject_mismatches=1 -- but the verifier is harness/provenance/interface.py, this platform's own code, which is the misaligned half: verification requires a checker from this platform. The signature is an hmac-sha256 over the pre-authentication encoding, so the 'public key material' a third party would hold is the signing secret itself, and the repository reports this honestly rather than claiming otherwise (external_verifier_independent=False, and a report that falsely claimed independence fails the gate).
gap: No verification by a tool this repository did not write, and none is possible as built: the shared-secret MAC gives no public verifiability, and the run-output predicate type is an unregistered urn, so an off-the-shelf in-toto/DSSE verifier holding only the artifact, the envelope and public key material has neither a key it can check nor a predicate it can look up. Filling it means an asymmetric signer (the code says only mac() changes) plus a fetched foreign verifier exercised in the gate on both the passing and the mutated arm.

finding: Everything that actually signs here signs with a long-lived key this deployment holds: the default binding declares key_lifetime 'long-lived', and the wired boundary every real producing path calls hardcodes keyid local-held-key-v1 with no binding selection at all, which is the misaligned anchor's first half. The keyless shape exists and works -- the second binding signs the same closure as ephemeral:run-done-human-0001:2026-09-03T23:59:59Z and returns an inclusion proof -- but it is a per-run in-process identity with no identity provider or log behind it, and it is not what the platform's own emission path uses. On timing the picture is split: the wired boundary attests at the production choke point as the artifact is made, while this closing boundary signs attempts, costs and check reports the closure declares rather than observed, so that record is a report about work it did not watch.
gap: Keyless short-lived signing is modelled, not adopted: the emission boundary has no adapter seam, so the ephemeral-identity binding cannot be selected on the path the platform actually produces through, and neither an identity provider nor a transparency log is reached in either binding. The signed record of what an agent did is also assembled from declarations at closing time rather than captured at the action, so what is signed at that boundary is a report whoever submits the closure can shape.
